original_test_intent: Execute exactly one explicitly approved ComputerSystem.Reset action on the verified System and prove the ResetType-specific power, management and return-to-service outcome without losing diagnostic evidence.
original_method: Resolve the System action target and allowable ResetTypes, capture power/workload/log baselines, obtain final approval, POST one selected type using secure Redfish, poll bounded task/power/availability signals, and collect type-specific recovery evidence.
manual_activity: The owner selects an allowed ResetType and expected transition, confirms the exact System, maintenance/workload evacuation, outage window, console/out-of-band recovery and type-specific return-to-service criteria immediately before execution.
required_inputs: Immutable BMC/System identity and advertised Reset action target
Approved exact ResetType and expected state sequence
Trusted TLS and least-privilege action credential
safety_requirements: Do not use GET for the reset action
Do not assume Systems/1 or system
Do not default ResetType to On
No fixed sleep as sole verification
Stop on lost recovery access or unexpected state
No unrelated mutation or log clearing
agent_execution_scope: Validate System/action identity and allowable ResetTypes
Capture pre-action power, health, workload and log baseline
Archive preserved evidence and no-repeat audit
engineer_actions: Approve target, ResetType, outage and workload impact

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: POST is the correct action shape, but fixed `On`, guessed member identity, `-k`, password-on-command-line IPMI and a five-second delay do not establish the requested transition or recovery. Chassis status cannot prove host/service readiness.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After final approval, POST one firmware-allowed ResetType to the resolved action target with trusted TLS, capture any task response, and boundedly verify the expected power transition plus BMC, console, OS and workload return without retrying blindly.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The single ComputerSystem.Reset scope and 15/10 timing remain; no member, ResetType, delay, reboot semantics or recovery deadline is inferred.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use an action-schema-driven one-shot reset plan whose monitoring and success oracle are derived from the approved ResetType, not a generic sleep/chassis-status check.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Corrects the GET/POST conflict and fixed target/type, adds workload approval, preserved evidence, bounded task/state monitoring and explicit incident recovery.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Covers the chosen reset behavior only; other ResetTypes require separate approvals and expected state sequences.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Reset can interrupt workloads and unflushed I/O, alter boot timing or strand the host. BMC availability may survive while host recovery fails, so multiple independent readiness signals are required.

project_override_considerations: IPMI may be used only as an approved secret-safe cross-check, never as replacement action or sole recovery proof. A Redfish SDK is equivalent if it preserves action target, selected ResetType, response/task evidence and bounded state timeline.
expected_evidence: Immutable System/action identity, firmware and allowed ResetType list
Final owner approval, maintenance/workload clearance and recovery readiness
Redacted POST/task response and exact ResetType/timestamps
Bounded power and availability transition timeline
Preserved BMC/SEL/OS logs and no-repeat/no-unrelated-mutation audit

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The Master item explicitly says POST ComputerSystem.Reset, but its Procedure sends GET to the action URI. These methods have different semantics, and GET cannot perform the named reset. The conflict is preserved rather than silently accepting DeepSeek's chosen POST payload.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The reset purpose is explicit. Target resolution, allowed ResetType, approval, monitoring and recovery are concrete prerequisites; no action may run until they are supplied.

review_improvement: Turns a contradictory GET and guessed one-shot `On` request into a ResetType-specific, approved, observable and non-retrying system reset contract.
independent_technical_reasoning: ComputerSystem.Reset is an action whose same endpoint can represent materially different operations, from power-on to forced restart. Therefore neither the endpoint nor an HTTP success alone defines expected behavior. The allowed value must be discovered from the target schema, approved against current workload state, and paired with a transition timeline. A five-second pause and chassis status can miss delayed task acceptance, boot failure or service non-recovery, while automatic repetition could compound damage.
